scope_line: Scope: OpenHands/OpenHands (Agent Canvas front end) plus OpenHands/software-agent-sdk (SDK, agent server, tools, workspaces), because v0.3 requires assessing delegated capabilities where they live. OpenHands Cloud is out of scope.

A1.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

A2.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

A3.rationale: Agent runtime: generic business-object criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

B1.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

B2.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD criterion (fixed per-archetype rule).

B3.evidence: Typed client for the Agent Server API (src/api/open-hands.types.ts); the contract itself belongs to the Agent Server.

C1.evidence: Canvas extensions are specified to contribute routed pages, panels, renderers, slots and themes as installable packages (specs/canvas-extensions.md), partly shipped behind capability detection; core layout is code.
C1.alt_note: Once shipped, extensions are validated, installable layout data.

C2.rationale: Agent runtime: generic CRUD views (fixed per-archetype rule).

C3.evidence: Colour themes are palette definitions covering interface, code and terminal (src/themes/README.md); eight locale files.

D1.evidence: Automations with cron and event triggers, templates and git sync are defined in the UI (src/types/automation.ts:3-13, src/routes/automation-*.tsx); they run on a separate automation server.

D2.evidence: The agent server posts events to configured webhooks with buffering and retries (openhands-agent-server/openhands/agent_server/config.py:73-104).

D3.evidence: Hooks run at defined points (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/hooks); agent actions run in Docker, Apptainer, cloud or remote workspaces (openhands-workspace/openhands/workspace), but hook isolation and egress control were not verified.
D3.alt_note: If hooks execute inside the sandboxed workspace.

E1.evidence: Component library with accessibility lint rules (eslint.config.js); no automated accessibility scans.
E1.alt_note: If lint rules without scans count as no automation.

E2.evidence: No audit store in the canvas; durable audit is documented only through an external DefenseClaw integration (docs/DefenseClaw.md).

E3.evidence: Telemetry is consent-gated with opt-out (src/services/telemetry.ts:9-29); there is no data export or erasure feature in the canvas.
E3.alt_note: Consent management is a privacy control, though not export or erasure.

E4.evidence: No security scanning in CI; runtime security is delegated to the Agent Server or external guardrails (docs/DefenseClaw.md).

F1.evidence: Automation definitions sync to git (src/routes/automation-git-sync.tsx); other settings are unversioned.

F3.evidence: Confirmation policies (never, always, confirm risky) decide which agent actions need a person (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/security/confirmation_policy.py:27-43); they govern actions, not changes to the agent itself.

F4.evidence: CI checks REST API breakage, persisted-settings compatibility and deprecations on every change (software-agent-sdk .github/workflows/agent-server-rest-api-breakage.yml, persisted-settings-compat.yml, deprecation-check.yml).

G1.rationale: Agent runtime: generic-store query performance (fixed per-archetype rule).

G2.evidence: Single user by default, with a Helm chart for team deployments (helm/agent-canvas).

G3.evidence: No performance suite or documented limits (searched for benchmark, load test and perf).

H1.evidence: The canvas deploys separately from the Agent Server and Automation Server behind an API contract, as an npm library, desktop app, container and Helm chart (docs/architecture.md, electron/, docker/, helm/).

H2.evidence: Library entrypoints and lint configuration; no architectural boundary tests.

H3.evidence: Lint, unit tests and builds on Ubuntu and Windows plus mocked-LLM Playwright E2E on pull requests (.github/workflows/ci.yml:4-66, mock-llm-e2e.yml); mutation testing (stryker.config.mjs); no accessibility or security checks.
H3.alt_note: Coverage is broad, including mutation testing.

I1.evidence: Skills, plugins and MCP servers are configured through the canvas (src/routes/skills-plugins.tsx, mcp-settings.tsx); canvas extensions for UI are partly shipped.
I1.alt_note: Once extensions ship, UI, layout and theme are all plugin points.

I2.evidence: No isolation model for canvas extensions is evidenced; agent code isolation is delegated to backends.

I3.evidence: Mocked-LLM development server and seed scripts (scripts/seed-automation-ux-data.mjs, docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).

K1.evidence: The canvas consumes MCP and exposes a UI tool that lets agents drive the canvas (tools/canvas_ui_tool.py); no MCP server for the canvas itself.

K2.evidence: Users run agent conversations with actions through the canvas; there is no natural-language authoring of canvas definitions.

K3.evidence: The default confirmation policy is NeverConfirm (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/conversation/state.py:123); with ConfirmRisky, LLM security analyzers classify each action's risk and risky ones pause for a person (security/llm_analyzer.py, toolshield_llm_analyzer.py, ensemble.py).

N1.evidence: OpenHands, Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and other ACP agents map onto one agent protocol, so adding an agent is configuration (docs/ACP_AGENTS.md).

N2.evidence: Backends (local, Docker, VM, cloud) and ACP agents are configurable; no connector SDK with lifecycle.
N2.alt_note: ACP is a standard connector definition.

N3.evidence: Relies on the versioned Agent Server API and ACP; no deprecation windows in the canvas.

O1.evidence: Kernel of conversations, backends, automations, profiles and skills with no business-domain nouns; channels exist only as automation outputs.

O2.evidence: Automation templates cover new tasks without kernel change (src/routes/automation-templates.tsx).

O3.evidence: Automation templates and git sync; installable canvas extensions are partly shipped.

J1.evidence: Consent-gated product analytics to PostHog (src/services/telemetry.ts); not available to product features.

J2.evidence: No typed feedback or learning signals in the canvas or the SDK.

J3.evidence: No joined mining in the canvas.

M1.evidence: No proposals for changing the canvas.

M3.evidence: Automations run coding agents on schedules and events for narrow tasks such as decomposing GitHub issues (README).

M4.evidence: No binding of changes to baselines or metrics.

L1.evidence: Backend server_info with runtime services (docs/architecture.md) and container health in the entrypoint (docker/entrypoint.sh).

L2.evidence: Docker, Helm and desktop builds; mocked-LLM Docker E2E stands up an environment per run (.github/workflows/mock-llm-docker-e2e.yml).

L3.evidence: Playwright journeys with mocked and live configurations and a testing matrix (docs/TESTING_MATRIX.md); no changed-path map or adoption instrumentation.
L3.alt_note: The testing matrix maps surfaces to journeys.

P1.evidence: No learning from sessions was found in the SDK (searched openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/skills, context, agent).

P2.evidence: Critics evaluate task output for iterative refinement (openhands-sdk/openhands/sdk/critic), not changes to the agent itself.

limits: Repository evidence only, at the two tips named above. OpenHands Cloud is out of scope. Hook isolation was not verified. Single rater.
reading: **With the SDK in scope:** webhooks with retries (D2 3), automated compatibility checks in CI (F4 3), and risk-classifying confirmation policies that are available but off by default (K3 2, 3 with ConfirmRisky). **Largest gap:** Learning (1.0). Critics refine task output, but nothing learns from sessions (P1 1).
